outcome: Give hospital coo / chief medical information officer a governed method to improve door-to-clinician median minutes using arrival histories, acuity scores and staffed beds, with final decisions…
overview: Emergency Department Patient Flow Forecasting addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in healthcare providers operations. The first proof of value uses arrival histories, acuity scores and staffed beds. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is door-to-clinician median minutes, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: arrival histories, acuity scores and staffed beds; define door-to-clinician median minutes and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hospital COO / Chief Medical Information Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for door-to-clinician median minutes
